mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is not below the 5th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and capacity utilization, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% signals robust labor market expansion, boosting consumer demand and corporate profits, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is not above the 95th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% in the same month signals a dual tightening in monetary policy and inflation, increasing real interest rates and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered months (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is not below the 10th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 2% over three consecutive months, alongside a decline in consumer spending growth (proxied by GDPC1), signals a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in demand-driven equities and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +2% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 growth < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is not below the 25th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over four consecutive months signals a manufacturing recovery, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained INDPRO growth (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is not above the 75th percentile of historical returns.
